v.why: Raising an already large learning rate pushes training into divergence (e.g. runs 48, 58, 60 show drops of 30-65 points).
At very small learning rates, 243 epochs underfit, so a larger step helps (runs 41, 42, 43).
Lowering a divergent learning rate recovers training, with gains up to +68 points (runs 49, 50).
Shallower nets are more stable at high learning rates (runs 93, 98, 91).
Deeper nets amplify instability at high learning rates (runs 88, 96).
With a tiny learning rate, wider layers learn faster and reduce underfitting (runs 74, 61).
Very small batches give noisy updates, and a larger batch stabilizes them (runs 22, 38, 21).
Strong L2 penalty underfits, so weakening it helps (runs 6, 14, 15).
More update steps per epoch at a high learning rate cause divergence (runs 28, 24).
Narrower layers reduce instability at high learning rates (runs 68, 79).
